key_insight: At high pressures, common LES-FMDF molecular mixing models can substantially mispredict conditional scalar diffusion because their mixing frequency does not scale correctly with pressure and diffusion physics.
engineering_relevance: This matters for high-pressure turbulent combustion and reacting-flow simulations, where inaccurate subgrid mixing can distort scalar transport, reaction rates, and design predictions.
method: Built a DNS database for spatially evolving turbulent slot jets of C7H16/O2 and C7H16/air.
Computed exact FMDF conditional scalar diffusion from DNS and compared it a priori against IEM, Modified Curl, and Mapping Closure models.
Studied pressures from 1 to 100 atm, with Reynolds numbers 850 and 1300, using compressible reacting-flow physics and real-gas thermodynamics.
evidence_signal: The evaluation uses DNS-derived FMDF and CSD across multiple pressures, filter widths, and spatial locations, showing significant model deviations at high pressure.
watch_item: The main limitation is that model performance is highly sensitive to the chosen mixing frequency, so pressure-dependent calibration may be required before use in real high-pressure LES-FMDF cases.
paper_title: Assessment of subgrid scale mixing models used in LES at high pressures
